identity.name: Polyphosphates
identity.chemical_class: Inorganic condensed phosphates (polyphosphates; linear/cyclic oligomers and polymers of orthophosphate)

function.mechanism: Polyphosphates chelate metal ions and alter ionic balance, supporting emulsification, water binding, texture control, and formulation stability.

adi.basis: EFSA 2019 group ADI for phosphates (E338-341, E343, E450-452), expressed as phosphorus.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no genotoxicity/carcinogenicity concern in the phosphate group but found modeled ADI exceedance in younger and high-intake populations, including supplement scenarios.

fda.notes: In cited sections, substances are GRAS when used in accordance with good manufacturing practice (GMP); current eCFR HTML pages were bot-protected, so official eCFR API text was used.

adi.basis: JECFA group MTDI for phosphorus from all sources, expressed as P; E452 entries list MTDI 70 mg/kg bw (as P).

concerns.summary: EFSA exposure modeling showed ADI exceedance in several younger/high-intake groups, and recent literature highlights potential risk from high inorganic phosphate additive exposure in phosphate-sensitive populations.
Mechanistic review literature proposes cardiorenal pathways (vascular calcification and mineral-hormone dysregulation) linking high inorganic phosphate additive exposure to adverse outcomes.
A 2025 animal study reported anxiety-like behavior with high dietary phosphate intake; relevance to typical human E452 exposure remains uncertain.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA reported no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity in the phosphate additive group dataset.
EFSA reported no developmental toxicity effects in studies reviewed for the phosphate group.
No IARC monograph classification entry was identified for E452-related names in the checked IARC classification resources.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2019 reported modeled exceedance of the group ADI (40 mg/kg bw/day as P) in multiple younger and high-intake scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E452 remains authorized in EU/U.S./JECFA frameworks, but EFSA established a finite group ADI and reported exceedance in several younger/high-intake groups; human and mechanistic studies support caution at elevated inorganic phosphate additive exposure.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI 40 mg/kg bw/day (as phosphorus)
EFSA-reported ADI exceedance in infants/toddlers/children and high-consuming adolescents
FDA GRAS status for related condensed phosphate ingredients under GMP in 21 CFR Part 182
JECFA MTDI 70 mg/kg bw/day (as P) for phosphate group
No IARC Group 1/2A/2B classification found for E452-related names in checked IARC resources
